subject: Capacity sprint — aligning OEM quotes & cloud reserve for OrbitAI (DEAL-7843)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@orbitai.com>, sales@prime-oem.com, procurement@nimbuscloud.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity sprint — aligning OEM quotes & cloud reserve for OrbitAI (DEAL-7843)

Elaine / partners,

Thanks for the productive sync last week. OrbitAI's ramp (Q2/Q3 delivery windows) is now firming up and we need to lock a pragmatic procurement and backfill plan that keeps their onboarding SLOs intact while hedging for OEM lead-time risk. High level asks below — please respond with concrete items by COB Jan 12 so we can finalize the mutual action plan.

Immediate asks:
- Firm lead times by SKU (exact model/qty) and earliest partial-delivery milestones from Prime-OEM. If different SKUs map to the same procurement queue, call it out.
- Nimbus: confirm reserved capacity windows, minimum commit, and a short-term hourly backfill rate for on-demand usage (we need a 90-day bridge price).
- All parties: list cancellation penalties, change-order lead times, and whether pre-shipment inspections or customs add contingency days.

Risk scenarios we want covered (examples):
1) OEM ETA +21 days variance — what partial shipments can we expect and when?
2) OEM queue slips beyond Q3 — what cloud reserve capacity can Nimbus commit and at what discount?
3) If incremental SKU substitution is needed (e.g., slightly different GPU gen), who certifies perf/regression and how long does requalification take?

Attachments: I’ve attached the latest draft of OrbitAI's expected consumption curve and a blank mutual action plan template.

Proposed timeline:
- Jan 12: vendor responses + pricing
- Jan 15: internal decision on hybrid model (partial OEM commit + Nimbus bridge)
- Jan 20: doc signatures / PO issued

Ben / Neha / Jonas — please review and flag any missing procurement/legal constraints.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Dedicated Capacity, Redwood Inference

Attachments: orbitai_consumption_curve.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.docx
From: Elaine Park <elaine@orbitai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, sales@prime-oem.com
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sprint — aligning OEM quotes & cloud reserve for OrbitAI (DEAL-7843)

Karthik —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick responses inline:

- Prime-OEM (copying their sales): current ETA for the 80-card tranche is ~14–18 weeks from PO for the quoted SKU (Prime A100-768GB). We can stage a 30-card partial shipment at ~10–12 weeks if you’re comfortable taking a mixed SKU lane (we can offer an A100-lite config for the partial). Full updated quote attached (orbitai_oem_quote_v3.pdf).

- Nimbus: we can commit a 60-day reserved window with a guaranteed floor for 50% of the ramped baseline. Short-term hourly bridge rate is attached (nimbus_capacity_offer.xlsx). We can extend to 90 days with an additional 12% blended fee.

- Cancellation / change order: Prime-OEM's standard policy is 25% restocking for cancellations within 30 days of ship, otherwise pro-rated. Customs / inspection add 5–7 business days typical, but we can expedite at cost.

Open Q: can Redwood accept mixed-SKU staging (partial A100-lite) for the initial tranche while full SKU arrives? That would reduce lead-time exposure and fit OrbitAI's earliest critical path.

Happy to hop on a short working session tomorrow to run permutations.

Best,
Elaine Park
VP, Platform @ OrbitAI

Attachments: orbitai_oem_quote_v3.pdf, nimbus_capacity_offer.xlsx
From: procurement@nimbuscloud.com <procurement@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@orbitai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 13:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sprint — aligning OEM quotes & cloud reserve for OrbitAI (DEAL-7843)

Hi Karthik / Elaine —

Nimbus confirms the capacity offer that Elaine summarized. Key points:
- 60-day bridge: guaranteed pool of virtual GPUs equivalent to 50% of projected baseline, hourly bridge rate as attached.
- 90-day extension: additional 12% fee (one-time) to keep priority allocation in our reservoir.
- Onboarding ETA: we can provision the bridge pool within 48 hours of contract signature; full reserved infra (customer-dedicated nodes) requires 14–21 days for placement.
- Support SLA: 99.5% uptime for the bridge (standard) with optional 24/7 dedicated channel for an uplift.

We logged the provisional hold against OrbitAI starting Jan 10; hold valid for 7 days pending signed MSA or PO.

If Redwood wants to formalize a hybrid approach (partial OEM + Nimbus bridge), we recommend accepting the partial shipments option from Prime-OEM and signing the 60-day bridge to remove queue pressure.

Regards,
Nimbus Procurement Team
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jan 2028 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sprint — aligning OEM quotes & cloud reserve for OrbitAI (DEAL-7843)

Thanks for the vendor replies — good signal. Quick internal take and recommendation: accept the mixed-SKU partial tranche + Nimbus 60-day bridge, with the following guardrails so we don’t expose OrbitAI to perf regressions or cost surprises:

Action items / guardrails:
- Accept Prime-OEM partial (30 cards A100-lite) conditional on a short perf smoke test: Redwood-run perf validation within 5 business days of partial delivery; if regressions >7% on key prompts, hold invoice until remediation or credit.
- Execute Nimbus 60-day bridge; negotiate 90-day extension as an option (don’t commit cashfully). Have legal add a clause to convert bridge hours to reserved credits if OEM delay >45 days.
- Procurement: push Prime-OEM for a stamped PO with clear ship milestones, and invoice split by tranche.
- Legal: SOW/Master services addendum to cover substitution SKU and acceptance tests.

Neha / Jonas — can you 1) confirm we can schedule the perf smoke test within 5 business days and 2) confirm finance terms (split invoice acceptance / escrow) by EOD Jan 10? If yes, I’ll instruct procurement to accept the partial tranche and lock Nimbus hold.

-Ben
Director, Capacity Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@orbitai.com>, procurement@nimbuscloud.com, sales@prime-oem.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jan 2028 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sprint — aligning OEM quotes & cloud reserve for OrbitAI (DEAL-7843)

All —

Confirmed: procurement and finance can proceed on the proposed hybrid route if the following are in place by COB Jan 10:
- Signed PO for partial tranche with shipment milestones and split invoicing (Procurement lead: Jonas Weber).
- Legal to draft a short addendum that mandates a Redwood perf smoke test window (5 business days) and remediation credit if regressions >7% (Legal looped in separately).
- Nimbus: provide a short amendment that allows conversion of unused bridge hours to reserved credits if OEM delay >45 days.

Jonas — please take the lead on stamping the PO and capture Prime-OEM ship milestones. I’ll coordinate with finance to set the escrow terms and payment schedule.

Elaine / Nimbus team — we’ll route the mutual_action_plan.docx back to you (filled) once the PO language is finalized; please keep the Nimbus hold active through Jan 17 while we finalize signatures.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference
